# #945 — 878 done-means clause 2 judges the import's line shape: a prettier-wrapped require-test-database import fails a file that demands the database

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: bug
Created: 2026-08-28T02:39:16Z
Updated: 2026-08-28T02:39:16Z

---

Found by the session-10 lanes for backup-restore-live (pull request #944) and reported first by the phase-1 lane.

scripts/done-means/878-pg-tests-require-database.sh clause 2 demands the helper identifier (requireTestDatabaseUrl | requireLocalCloneTestDatabaseUrl | requireScratchAdminUrl) and the module basename require-test-database on ONE import line. A file importing two of the helpers gets its import wrapped by prettier in the pre-commit gate onto several physical lines, and clause 2 then reports FAIL while clauses 1, 3, and 4 all PASS: the file demands the database and hard-fails without it, and the check says it does not. The lanes worked around it with one named specifier per import line (the origin/main convention), which is fine as a convention but is not what the clause claims to check.

Second shape of the same defect: a split half that reaches the helper only through a shared lane helper module (which imports it) fails clause 2 too, though clause 3 proves the hard fail; each half now carries its own call and single-line import.

Ask: make clause 2 match the identifier and the basename within the same import STATEMENT (multi-line aware), or document the one-specifier-per-line convention in the script header and in HANDOVER-RULES; prove it with a deliberate miss per rule 40 (a wrapped import that should pass, and a file with no import that should fail).

Parent: #878. Related: #918 (clause design), #944.
